metadata.why_justification: The contract document pins this header line character for character, so a renamed or resequenced field breaks the layout the corrections desk is sent. Entailed by: "Header, exactly: `claim_id,true_average,true_count,driver`"

metadata.how_justification: Parses claim_register.csv with csv.read_rows and applies table_equals to every graded cell of the RC-07 row (matched by 'claim_id'); the row is graded here and NOWHERE else, the bulk check below carrying only its id in the population lock; a failure names the exact cell.
metadata.why_justification: Every claim is verified on three axes at once: the store's real average, the store's real count, and which of the two — if either — the article got wrong. The article's own order governs the line-up as well, so a claim dropped from the register, one duplicated inside it, one resequenced against the article, and a listing the article never quotes smuggled in beside them each fail here. The two figures are graded beside the driver, cell by cell, because a driver stripped of the figure behind it is not something a corrections desk can act on. Entailed by: "One row per claim in `input/claims.csv`, in that file's order — every claim earns a row, the ones the store bears out among them. `true_average` is the store's real average for that listing under `input/verification_rules.md`, written to one decimal place (`4.0`, not `4`). `true_count` is the store's real number of ratings for it, a plain whole number with no separator. `driver` is one of the four codes above, spelled exactly as it is spelled there."

metadata.how_justification: Parses claim_register.csv with csv.read_rows and applies table_equals: every graded cell of 14 rows plus the full 15-row population as a row_set lock (duplicate-row and cross-product dumps fail the lock; a duplicated graded id is rejected outright), the delivered row order equal to the stated order, and the delivered column set closed to the stated header, with declared cell types {'true_average': 'number', 'true_count': 'number', 'driver': 'text'} normalised on both sides. A failure names the exact row and column.

metadata.why_justification: The corrections note reached the workspace.

metadata.how_justification: Opens verification_note.md with md.extract_text and applies regex_match.
metadata.why_justification: The note is sent to a corrections desk, so it has to be sentences somebody wrote rather than a handful of codes and tallies; a thin note loses weight here rather than failing.

metadata.how_justification: Opens verification_note.md with md.extract_text and applies regex_match.
metadata.why_justification: The note says of the claim carrying the largest count gap — the one the verification turns on — that its `driver` is COUNT_WRONG, naming it by the `claim_id` the article's list spells and putting that code in the same paragraph, with neither another code nor the id of a claim coded differently standing between them. A note that names the claim while calling it right, and a note that lists the ids and the codes without joining them up, both fail here. Both names stand in the same paragraph: this is CO-NAMING, not attribution. Which record carries which value is pinned cell by cell in the register and in results.json, both core.

metadata.how_justification: Opens verification_note.md with md.extract_text and applies regex_match.
metadata.why_justification: The note says of the one claim whose weighted mean sits exactly on a half that its `driver` is AVERAGE_WRONG — the claim the rounding rule alone decides, and the one a solver who rounds to the even digit or cuts the mean short reports as right. Naming it beside the wrong code, or beside no code, is the reading this refuses. Both names stand in the same paragraph: this is CO-NAMING, not attribution. Which record carries which value is pinned cell by cell in the register and in results.json, both core.

metadata.how_justification: Opens verification_note.md with md.extract_text and applies regex_match.
metadata.why_justification: The note stands the number of rows its own register codes NOTHING_WRONG beside the heading **confirmed in full**, or beside the shorter spelling of it the contract names. The heading is matched across exactly the renderings `input/submission_format.md` names for it — clause order, an inserted article or auxiliary, a singular or plural head, and the short spellings it discloses — and across those only: this reads a stated heading in its own words, never a synonym of the writer's choosing, and the contract says so rather than inviting a rewording it cannot honour. It loses weight rather than failing, because results.json already pins the same number and a fair writer's phrasing must not veto a perfect register.
